title: The director behind the action
category: dictionary-labelled Dhaga headword idiom; source-informed editorial reading
literal_meaning: Gobardhan Das, the master of the play.
explanation: The dictionary defines a concealed controller: others visibly act, while this person directs them. The theatrical wording identifies the person behind the action, not a documented theatre practitioner. Our application asks who actually makes a decision when somebody else announces it; hidden direction need not be guessed from appearances alone.
meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଏମିତି ଜଣେ ସୂତ୍ରଧରଙ୍କୁ ବୁଝାଏ, ଯିଏ ନିଜେ ଚିହ୍ନା ନପଡ଼ି ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ କାମକୁ ଚଳାନ୍ତି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ହେଉଛି—ଖବର ଦେଉଥିବା ଲୋକ ଓ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେଉଥିବା ଲୋକ କିଏ? କେବଳ ଚେହେରା ଦେଖି ଲୁଚା ସୂତ୍ରଧର ଥିବାର ଅନୁମାନ କରିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: A named theatrical idiom points to concealed direction behind visible action.
odia_summary: ଆଗରେ କାମ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପଛରେ ଥିବା ସୂତ୍ରଧରକୁ ଏହି ପଦଟି ବୁଝାଏ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ମୀନା ସଭାରେ ନୂଆ ସମୟ ଘୋଷଣା କଲେ। ରବି ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଏହି ସମୟ କିଏ ଠିକ୍ କଲା?” ମୀନା ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତିର ଚିଠି ଦେଖାଇଲେ। / Meena announced a new meeting time. Ravi asked who had chosen it, and she showed him the decision letter. This invented scene explores responsibility; it does not establish a secret plot.
cultural_context: The source labels the whole headword Dhaga and supplies its figurative meaning. Gobardhan Das remains part of the expression; this page does not identify a historical individual, author or origin. Bengali and Hindi equivalents are listed, not evidence of transmission direction.
